attributes.body_ja:
「きり」は、五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「切（き）る」から生（う）まれた表現（ひょうげん）です。動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）や名詞（めいし）、または数詞（すうし）のあとに付（つ）いて、その出来事（できごと）や数量（すうりょう）だけに限（かぎ）る副助詞（ふくじょし）として働（はたら）きます。まずは、動詞（どうし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）う「きり」の例（れい）を見（み）てみましょう。

「きり」を動詞（どうし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）う場合（ばあい）は、主（おも）に「(A) が一度（いちど）起（お）こってから、その状態（じょうたい）が続（つづ）いている」ことを意味（いみ）します。

「きり」が名詞（めいし）や数詞（すうし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）は、「(A) だけ」で、それ以上（いじょう）でもそれ以下（いか）でもないことを表（あらわ）します。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「きり」は「っきり」や「キリ」と表現（ひょうげん）されることもあります。この場合（ばあい）も特（とく）にニュアンスは変（か）わりません。ただし、くだけた場面（ばめん）では「っきり」がよく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
As an adverbial particle, きり may convey that 'upon (A)', where (A) is usually a verb, that action was the 'first and last time'. This is frequently translated as 'only', 'just', or 'since'. きり comes from the う - Verb 切（き）る 'to cut'. きり is often used after the plain past form of verbs, with nouns, or with counters. Let's look at verbs first.

With verbs, きり is primarily used to show that (A) occurring was all that was required for (B). Usually, this results in some permanent consequence, or permanent change of opinion. In almost every situation, (A) is something that has only happened once, and きり can be interpreted as 'ever since'.

When it comes to the use of きり with nouns or counters, it will express that something is happening with (A) as the limit 'nothing more, nothing less'. In other words, (A) is all that will be included in some particular situation/action.

Caution

きり may also be seen as っきり or キリ. There is no specific change in nuance, but っきり is the most common casual form.

きり often marks an action done once and left that way, as in 去年会ったきり連絡がない ('I haven't heard from them since we met last year'). まま(に) marks an ongoing unchanged state, as in 靴を履いたまま入らないで ('Don't enter with your shoes on'). Both can imply continuation, but きり emphasizes a cutoff point.

second_relatable.title: まま(に)
second_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

attributes.body: Both を限りに  and きり mark a point after which something stops or changes, but they differ in formality and nuance. を限りに is a fixed, formal expression used mainly in written or public contexts to indicate a clear and definitive final point, often for events, careers, or official actions, as in 本日を限りに閉店します (‘As of today, we will close for good.’). In contrast, きり is more casual and flexible, commonly used in everyday speech to say that something has not happened again since a certain point, and often used with number + counter expressions such as 一度きりしか会っていない ('I haven't met him except that one time.')

first_relatable.title: を限りに
first_relatable.meaning: As of (the end of), (Starting) from, (No longer) after, By (the), Ending with

attributes.body: きり and だけしか both express limitation, but with different nuance. きり often implies that something has happened only once or hasn't changed since, e.g. 去年会ったきり一度も連絡が来ない 'I haven't heard from them even once since we met last year.' だけしか means 'Nothing but', typically in a way that emphasizes lack or even disappointment, e.g. 千円だけしか持っていない 'I only have 1000 yen.'

だけ means 'only' or 'just,' while きり has a more specific nuance. After a past tense verb, きり suggests a permanent change after an event. For example, 日本に行ったきり、戻ってこなかった means 'Once (he) went to Japan, he never returned.' When used after a number + counter (e.g. 一人きり), it emphasizes 'nothing more, nothing less.'

たなり・なり and きり are very similar in meaning, both expressing that a certain state persists without the expected result occurring, and are often interchangeable. For example, in '東京に行ったきり地元に帰って来なかった' ('Once he went to Tokyo, he never came back to his hometown') and '東京に行ったなり地元に帰って来なかった' both convey the same lingering, unresolved situation.

first_relatable.title: たなり・なり
first_relatable.meaning: While... ~ing, Remaining, Not or ever since, Keep or leave

attributes.body: きり and しか～ない can both express the idea of 'only,' but in different ways. きり is used primarily with number+counter expressions, like 一度きり 'only one time' or 二人きり 'only/just the two of us'. In contrast, しか～ない is used with a noun and negative verb to mean 'only' or 'nothing but', e.g. １００円しかない ('I have only 100 yen.'). In some cases, the two can be used together, e.g. 一度きりしか行っていない ('I only went just the once.').
